chunks: Ali ibn Isma'il from Hammad from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That Barirah had a husband who was a slave, so when she was freed, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to her, 'Choose.'

key_terms.بَرِيرَةَ: Barirah, a well-known freed slave woman in Islamic history

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the marriage of a freed slave woman (Umm Walad or just freed) with her slave husband in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the juristic principle of *ikhtiyar* (autonomous choice) for a freed slave woman, distinguishing her status from that of a free woman whose marriage is not automatically dissolved upon emancipation. The Prophet’s directive to Barirah highlights her legal agency to validate or annul the marriage contract with her former slave husband, a precedent widely cited in Shia fiqh regarding the conditions of manumission and marital continuity.
